limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that the finish gate's verdict reflects what `make verify` returned. Each case is a tiny repository whose lint, test and typecheck targets are all green and whose verify target reds; the gate must say `fail`. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: anything about the RUNNER lane. These cases set FLOW_GATE_CPP_DIR to empty, which forces the Makefile fallback - the only lane reachable from a fixture, since the runner lane needs a CPP checkout and `uv` resolving a real project. The runner half (verify declared with `gate=True` in the finish plan, and the shell reading the gate set out of the runner JSON rather than restating it) is pinned by tests/test_flow_finish_gate.py and tests/test_runner.py instead. It also establishes nothing about `make verify` itself; what verify checks is its own subject, and row 40 of the census is where that question lives. `make` IS ABSENT FROM THE NEGATIVE-CONTROLS CI IMAGE - checked against ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.11-bookworm-slim rather than assumed - so each case carries its own `bin/make` and prepends it to PATH. Prepends, never replaces: the gate calls grep, sed, awk, mktemp and rm, and a PATH holding only the stub would make it fail to load, which is a different verdict reached for a reason that has nothing to do with this control. Only the EXECUTION is stood in for; the Makefile beside the stub is real text, and the gate greps it for `^verify:` exactly as it would in a real repository. TWO BAD CASES, one for each way a repository expresses a verification larger than the three gates: `bad-verify-reds` puts the failing checker in verify's own recipe, `bad-verify-only-checker-reds` reaches it through a prerequisite target nothing else runs. In both the anchor prints `FLOW_FINISH_GATE: ok` and exits 0 over a tree whose verification fails - a green that says nothing happened. A THIRD CASE WAS BUILT AND REJECTED, and the reason is worth keeping: it made verify an aggregate over `lint test typecheck extra-check`, which fires the #808 detector, so the anchor answered `warn (not run by fallback: extra-check)` - a true statement of its own ignorance offered in place of the answer it could have had by running the target. Rejected not because that is uninteresting but because it is UNSCORABLE: exit 3 without the declared signal cannot be confirmed as a MISS rather than a crash, and the harness reports UNRESOLVED rather than guessing. The distinction that case would have drawn is pinned in tests/test_flow_finish_gate.py instead, where the marker text can be read directly. It is also why the detect signal is `fail` alone and never `fail|warn`: widening it would make the anchor's honest warn score as a detection. THE GOOD CASE IS THE SAME TREE WITH A GREEN VERIFY, so the anchor agreeing there is what stops `always fail` satisfying this control. ISOLATION (attachment coupling, 2026-09-22): cases run through the shared runner controls/flow-finish-gate/run-case.sh, which copies the case outside every git repository before running the gate. They previously ran IN PLACE inside this checkout, so the gate read the ENCLOSING repository's git state - a fact the fixture never chose - looked for a counter-model receipt on that branch, found none, and this control's GOOD case failed. Measured at one sha: attached to a branch -> fail, DETACHED at the same sha -> ok, attached to main -> fail. ATTACHMENT is the variable, so main fails permanently and CI, always detached, can never see it. Only GOOD cases were contaminated: a failing gate step short-circuits before the counter-model check, so every BAD case redded correctly in place. NO detect_signal CHANGED in that work - the anchor causes none of these failures and -derivation is anchored AND passed both ways, which refutes it as the cause. DETECT_SIGNAL CHANGED, and ONLY because a committed case forced it. The pattern was END-ANCHORED `^FLOW_FINISH_GATE: fail$`, which cannot match any refusal carrying a reason - and the gate's own header at scripts/flow-finish-gate.sh:149-159 already RECORDED that constraint, saying any appended detail breaks this control and -derivation. The gate then appends detail on exactly one path (line 331, `fail (counter-model line <state>)`), so the documented constraint was already violated by the gate itself. That was LATENT while the controls ran in place, because attachment made that path fail the GOOD case before any BAD case could reach it. probe-articulate-refusal-must-read-as-detected reaches it deliberately: an isolated fixture carrying a receipts directory with no matching receipt, which yields `fail (counter-model line unknown)`. With the anchor that case scored UNSIGNALLED - indistinguishable from a crash - so the loosening is justified BY the case rather than by judgement. `\b` and not `.*`: the companion fixture cases/probe-crash-must-not-read-as-detected is a gate that dies by signal with exit 137 and NO verdict line, and tests pin that it still does not read as detection, which is the defect one layer down that a looser pattern would create. THE REAL-REPO PATH IS PINNED BY A TEST, NOT BY A CASE, and that is a measured limit rather than a preference (counter-model review, codex, MEDIUM). A case on the real path was written first and WITHDRAWN: with its planted defect entirely removed - every gate passing - it still emitted `FLOW_FINISH_GATE: fail` and still matched, because the ENCLOSING repository has no counter-model receipt for the current branch. It could not tell its own planted defect from its neighbour's receipt state, which is the ownership question this repository's detector contract asks, and it had re-imported the very coupling the isolation removes - the guard against drift, contaminated by the thing it guards against. `detect_signal` is control-level, so no per-case expectation can express 'only this planted defect counts'. tests/test_flow_finish_gate.py asserts the real path instead, where the specific evidence CAN be asserted.

anchors.why: THE REAL ARTICLE, not a reconstruction: the finish gate exactly as it stood at af348f8, the tip this issue branched from, vendored byte-for-byte and unmodified. It needs no adaptation because the fixture supplies everything it reads - a Makefile in the cwd and a `make` on PATH - so it runs here the way it ran in the field. It MISSES both known-bad inputs the same way - `FLOW_FINISH_GATE: ok`, exit 0, over a tree whose verification fails - and agrees with the fixed gate on the known-good one. That the miss is SILENT in both is a property of the cases, not of the anchor: see `limits` for the variant where it warns instead, and why a warn cannot be scored as a confirmed miss. AF348F8 IS RECORDED AS THE FIELD INSTANCE, and recording a commit is doing something narrower than it looks: a control keyed to one commit stops discriminating the moment that commit's defect is fixed, because the anchor and the gate are then the same program and every case scores INERT. That is not a reason to avoid naming it - an unnamed anchor cannot be re-derived from git at all - but it is the reason the anchor is VENDORED rather than resolved from history at run time, and the reason this control's continued value rests on the cases, which describe a defect SHAPE (a gate reporting on a subset of the checks it claims to cover) that outlives the commit. A later gate regressing into that shape reds these same cases against this same anchor.
